title: Graceful KV downgrade, fragment rediscovery, and incremental prefill orchestration
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Large multi-tenant workloads with paged attention see high variance in prefill latency and frequent noisy evictions when memory pressure interacts with eager prefill. Current eviction policies can cause long decode tail spikes when previously-evicted fragments are needed mid-decode. This ticket proposes a coordinated approach: graceful downgrade (soft-evict fences), fragment rediscovery (lightweight metadata bloom + rehydrate probes), and an incremental prefill orchestration layer that schedules topologically-important fragments first and opportunistically rehydrates nearby fragments while preserving low tail latency. Goals are to reduce decode-tail SLO violations, reduce wasted re-prefill work, and enable an ordered, latency-aware fallback when capacity is constrained.
acceptance_criteria: P99 decode latency for 99th percentile workloads reduced by >=20% compared to baseline under simulated memory pressure
Rehydrate-induced CPU/GPU overhead <= 3% of baseline across mixed workloads
Race conditions between soft-evict fencing and concurrent prefill resolved (no data corruption in 1M simulated traces)
Can roll back to existing eviction policy via a runtime flag without restarts
Operational dashboards to show: soft-evict events, fragment-rediscovery rate, rehydrate success rate, and kernel-hint hit ratio
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: RFC draft completed. Proposed components: soft-evict fence token, fragment bloom sketch for quick presence checks, ranked prefill planner, kernel-hint lane for rehydrate-friendly kernels.
2026-03-11: Spike 1 done - implemented prototype fence tokens in KV allocator; measured fence acquisition latency (median 35us, p99 140us) under synthetic load.

2026-03-12: Experiment A (baseline eviction vs soft-evict) on mixed-batch traffic: soft-evict reduced re-prefill frequency by 28% but increased transient memory high-water mark by 2.1%. Observed a pathological case when many small tenants simultaneously rehydrate — mitigation: staggered rehydrate backoff.

2026-03-13: Added heuristics to ranked prefill planner to prioritize fragments with high next-token hit-probability (using recency*access-frequency). Planned integration tests for race between fence release and prefill commit.
Next: implement opportunistic rehydrate probes (low-cost kernel hint path) and integrate with console dashboards; schedule canary on dedicated pool with strict SLOs.
implementation_notes: Soft-evict fence: allocate a small fence token per fragment on eviction; fences prevent immediate reuse of the same physical slot for unrelated fragments for a short window (configurable). Allows a lightweight rediscovery probe to check if decoders still expect fragment before destructive overwrite.

Fragment rediscovery: maintain a compact per-shard bloom sketch (rotating) and sequence number metadata for recent fragments. On cache miss, decoder issues rediscovery probe which consults bloom+seq to decide fast rehydrate vs full prefill.

Incremental prefill planner: accepts a list of candidate fragments ordered by predicted marginal decode benefit; schedules them in micro-batches to keep decode window steady while avoiding single large prefill storms.

Kernel hint lanes: expose a low-latency rehydrate path that uses lightweight kernel variants (reduced workspace, truncated compute) to warm KV pages with acceptable approximation; fallback to full kernel when hit probability validated.

Metrics and tracing: instrument fence lifecycle, rediscovery probe latencies, prefill planner decisions, and kernel-hint hits/misses. Add sampling for full trace capture when p99 latency spike occurs.
risks_and_mitigation: Increased memory high-water marks due to soft-evict fences — mitigation: adaptive fence TTL tuned by observed reuse rates and tenancy skew.
False positives in bloom-based rediscovery leading to wasted lightweight probes — mitigation: calibrate bloom size per shard and fall back to seq-checks for ambiguous cases.
Complexity in scheduler interactions with existing autoscaler — mitigation: conservative default (planner disabled) and gradual ramp via canary flag with observability gating.
Potential kernel correctness regressions for hint lanes — mitigation: unit + fuzz tests, canary on internal dedicated pool first, runtime flag to disable hint lanes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests, local cluster integration (3 nodes) - disable by default
Phase 1 (canary): enable on 1 dedicated pool behind a flag; collect metrics for 48h
Phase 2 (staged): enable for 10% of production traffic with runtime gating; verify SLOs for 7 days
Phase 3 (full): enable by default with adaptive fence TTL algorithm and monitoring alerts in place
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert if soft-evict events/frame > 5x baseline for 1m
Alert if rehydrate failure rate > 2% over 5m
Dashboard: rediscovery probe latency histogram, kernel-hint hit ratio over time, prefill planner queue length
